scenes.visualIntent: Problem-first hook introducing CBOT bond futures and multi-bond basket complexity
keyElements: Treasury bond futures allow delivery of many eligible bonds
Day count rules govern accrued interest between coupons
Conversion factors standardize diverse coupons at delivery

scenes.visualIntent: Compare Actual/Actual, 30/360, and Actual/360 day count rules
keyElements: US Treasury bonds accrue interest using Actual/Actual day counts
Corporate and municipal bonds follow standardized 30/360 months
Short-term money markets quote interest over 360-day years

scenes.visualIntent: Clarify clean screen quotes versus dirty cash settlement prices
keyElements: Clean price strips out accrued interest from trading screen quotes
Dirty price adds accrued interest to reflect true settlement cash
Cash price = Quoted clean price + Accrued interest

scenes.visualIntent: Explain the 15-year delivery basket and 6.0% yield Conversion Factor calibration
keyElements: CBOT allows delivery of non-callable bonds with >= 15 years maturity
Futures prices quote in points and 32nds per $100 par
Conversion Factor values each bond as if yielding 6.0% semi-annual

scenes.visualIntent: Deconstruct CBOT physical delivery cash equation
keyElements: Invoice Price scales settlement price by bond Conversion Factor
Accrued interest adds after scaling clean settlement price
Formula balances diverse bond coupons cleanly upon delivery

scenes.visualIntent: Compute Invoice Price for $90.00 settlement, CF 1.2000, and $2.50 accrued interest
keyElements: Multiply $90.00 settlement by CF 1.2000 to obtain $108.00
Add $2.50 accrued interest to arrive at $110.50 total cash
Invoice cash transfers clean value plus earned coupon days

scenes.visualIntent: Causal chain explaining how shorts identify the CTD bond in the basket
keyElements: Conversion factors match market yields cleanly only near 6.0%
Short traders minimize net delivery cost across eligible bonds
Futures quotes track the Cheapest-to-Deliver bond directly

scenes.visualIntent: Contrast which bond types become CTD when market yields rise above or fall below 6.0%
keyElements: Yields above 6.0% push low-coupon long-maturity bonds to CTD
Yields below 6.0% push high-coupon short-maturity bonds to CTD
Yield shifts across 6.0% rotate the optimal CTD bond

scenes.visualIntent: Illustrate the 2:00 PM settlement to 8:00 PM delivery notice Wild Card option
keyElements: Futures settlement locks daily at 2:00 PM Chicago time
Short sellers hold until 8:00 PM to file delivery notices
Afternoon yield spikes give shorts an asymmetric Wild Card profit

scenes.visualIntent: 3-beat quiz calculating Invoice Price for $95.00, CF 1.1000, Accrued $1.50
keyElements: Multiply $95.00 settlement by CF 1.1000 to obtain $104.50
Add $1.50 accrued interest for total invoice $106.00
Always apply Conversion Factor before adding accrued days

scenes.visualIntent: Synthesize Part 1 bond futures delivery rules and bridge to Part 2 Eurodollar & Duration Hedging
keyElements: Day counts and Conversion Factors standardize bond basket delivery
CTD minimization and Wild Card rules create short optionality
Part 2 next covers Eurodollar/SOFR, Convexity & Duration Hedging

scenes.visualIntent: Fixed 6-beat summary codifying all 8 rules of day counts and Treasury futures taught in Part 1
keyElements: Actual/Actual, 30/360, and Actual/360 govern bond accrual math
Invoice Price = Settlement * CF + Accrued
CTD rules and Wild Card timing favor the short seller
